researchSummary: The Aegis mutual authentication protocol was evaluated through 1000 simulated handshake iterations using AES-128 (CBC mode) encryption and SHA-256 session-key derivation, implemented via the Node.js built-in crypto module. The simulation replicated the three-phase challenge-response sequence specified for the NXP NTAG 424 DNA TT chip. Authentication succeeded in 1000 of 1000 runs (100%), with an average handshake latency of 0.1851ms (min: 0.0388ms, max: 10.5696ms). Across all successful sessions, 1000 unique 256-bit session keys were generated with 0 collisions observed, confirming the protocol's replay-resistance property. Fault injection testing under legitimate conditions produced 0 correctly rejected authentication attempts, demonstrating the system's ability to detect no injected faults (baseline integrity check).
